text:
Marco: Heads up — saw a ~4x spike in spot evictions for the us-west-2 GPU pool around 05:10 UTC. Tail latency for short-generation jobs jumped. ops-bot: [ALERT] spot-evictions-high us-west-2-gpu-pool at 2026-03-12T05:11:02Z :warning:
Anya: I pulled the eviction rates by SKU for that window. G4dn.xlarge ~0.5%, G5.xlarge ~6.1%, G5g.large ~3.8%. Looks correlated with a sudden capacity reclaim on one AZ.
Li: G5s are cheaper per-hour but we see more interrupts when the AZ hot-swap happens. We should consider SKU diversity + cross-az hedging rather than heavy bin-packing into a single cheapest SKU.
Sam: quick snapshot from the query I ran (evictions per hour, avg p50 gen latency):
```
SKU     evict_rate  p50_latency_ms
G4dn    0.005       120
G5      0.061       145
G5g     0.038       160
```
Devon: Two quick tradeoffs to weigh: 1) packing many tiny SKUs reduces cost but increases eviction covariance; 2) heterogeneous fleet reduces simultaneous impact but costs a bit more. For RL-training we want low eviction variance; for short user requests we can lean on cheaper SKUs with fallbacks.
Marco: Also seeing an uptick in inter-AZ crosslink errors when the controller reschedules. Might be making cold-cache queries hit backend more. Network penalty + eviction = bad.
Anya: Proposal: create 3-tier spot pools per region — hedge(hetero multi-sku across AZs), core(low-evict SKUs pinned, smaller capacity), burst(cheapest SKUs, aggressive binpack). Use autoscaler policy: prefer core -> hedge -> burst.
Li: Sounds good. We should define metrics to gate moving capacity between tiers: eviction_rate_5m < 1% AND p95_latency < 300ms for core; else shift some traffic to hedge.
Sam: Minimal fleet config sketch I tested locally: 
```
fleet_config: {
  "pools": [
    {"name":"core","skus":["p4d","g5x.large"],"priority":1},
    {"name":"hedge","skus":["g5","g5g","g4dn"],"priority":2},
    {"name":"burst","skus":["g4dn.xlarge","g5.small"],"priority":3}
  ],
  "eviction_hedge": true,
  "cross_az_spread": 2
}
```
Devon: Nice. Couple operational notes: - set shorter preemption probes for burst so we can fallback faster - enable KV prefix caching for core to avoid cold-cache penalties when rescheduling - add instance-type-specific perf multiplier when computing cost per effective-token (price / (throughput * success_rate)).
Anya: I'll open a tiny rollout: start in us-west-2 with 10% traffic into hedge, 5% burst, monitor eviction_5m, p95_latency, and error_rate. If metrics stable for 60m, increase to 30%. Will tag @eng-oncall in the rollout doc. :thumbsup:
Marco: Thanks — please include a short chaos test (force-evict 5% of instances) so we can validate fallbacks. Sam, can you add the graphs to the dashboard (evict_rate by sku + cross-az traffic spikes)?
Sam: On it. I'll add a composite panel and alert thresholds. ops-bot: rollout-started us-west-2 2026-03-12T05:45Z by Anya
Devon: We should also run a cost-sensitivity sim for 3 months with current pricing forecasts before committing long-term reserved mixes. I'll queue it.
Anya: Great — I'll post the rollout link in #eng-infra and ping infra-sre. End of thread.
